{
  "screen_decision": "include",
  "screen_rationale": "The study compares histopathological and transcriptome characteristics between a mouse model (GAN DIO-NASH mice) and human NASH patients, reporting quantitative measures of agreement in terms of gene expression overlap and histopathological scoring. It directly assesses the concordance between animal model results and human clinical outcomes.",
  "arm": "disease-biology",
  "arm_evidence": "The present study aimed to further validate the clinical translatability of GAN diet-induced liver lesions by comparing liver biopsy histopathological and transcriptome characteristics in GAN DIO-NASH mice and human NASH patients.",
  "therapeutic_areas": [
    "hepatic",
    "metabolic"
  ],
  "areas_evidence": "Non-alcoholic fatty liver disease (NAFLD) comprises a continuum of liver lesions ranging from simple steatosis to non-alcoholic steatohepatitis (NASH)... The presence of the metabolic syndrome, notably obesity and type 2 diabetes, is the strongest predisposing factor for development and progression of NAFLD.",
  "model_type": "induced",
  "model_evidence": "We have recently reported maintained fibrotic NASH histopathology in C57BL/6 J (GAN DIO-NASH) and ob/ob (GAN ob/ob ) mice fed a modified, trans-fat free AMLN diet termed the Gubra Amylin NASH (GAN) diet [ 22 ].",
  "species": [
    "mouse",
    "non-human-primate"
  ],
  "species_evidence": "The present study aimed to further validate the clinical translatability of GAN diet-induced liver lesions by comparing liver biopsy histopathological and transcriptome characteristics in GAN DIO-NASH mice and human NASH patients. ... Human subjects ... NASH patients (n = 16) were diagnosed and recruited at the Department of Hepatology and Gastroenterology, Aarhus University Hospital (Aarhus, Denmark). ... C57BL/6 J mice (5 weeks old) were from Janvier Labs...",
  "endpoint_class": "mixed",
  "endpoint_evidence": "The study compares histopathological scores (steatosis, inflammation, ballooning, fibrosis) and transcriptome data (differentially expressed genes, pathway analysis) between the mouse model and human patients."
}
